chunks: Do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner, until he reaches maturity; and give full measure and weigh with justice. We do not burden a soul beyond its capacity; and when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a relative. And fulfill the covenant of Allah. That is what He has enjoined upon you, that you may remember.
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical and economic commands regarding orphans, trade, and justice in this Quranic verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited as a comprehensive charter for social justice, emphasizing that protecting the vulnerable (orphans) and ensuring economic integrity (accurate measures) are acts of worship. The command to 'be just even if it concerns a relative' underscores the principle of impartiality in both legal and familial contexts, a key tenet in Shia jurisprudence. This passage serves as a foundational text for the concept of 'Adl' (Justice) in Islamic ethics, linking personal piety with societal equity.
